description: A composite of four bar-chart histograms in a 2x2 grid, lettered (a)-(d), each reporting the proportion distribution of austenitic grain size d obtained from EBSD on one intercritical quenched-annealed specimen of a low-density delta-TRIP steel. All four panels use identical axes: horizontal axis d/um with ten bins (<1.6, 1.6-2.0, 2.0-2.4, 2.4-2.8, 2.8-3.2, 3.2-3.6, 3.6-4.0, 4.0-4.4, 4.4-4.8, >4.8) and vertical axis Proportion/% spanning 0-40 with gridlines every 10. Panel (a) is labelled QA-620, (b) QA-680, (c) QA-740 and (d) QA-800 in the top-right corner of each panel (the caption instead writes "OA specimens", an apparent OCR/typing inconsistency). In every panel the distribution decreases monotonically with increasing grain size: the tallest bar is the <1.6 um bin (just below the 30 % gridline in a and b, at or slightly above 30 % in c and d), heights then fall bin by bin, and a small secondary rise reappears in the >4.8 um bin (below the 10 % gridline). No numeric data labels are printed; heights are read against the 10 % gridlines. The figure demonstrates that the fine-grained austenite statistics are essentially the same for all four annealing temperatures, i.e. most austenite grains are <2.0 um.

subfigures.description: Bar histogram labelled QA-620, Proportion/% (0-40) vs d/um. Tallest bar is the <1.6 um bin (just below the 30 % gridline), followed by 1.6-2.0 um (between 20 and 30 %); remaining bins fall progressively to 1-6 % with a small rise in the >4.8 um bin (below 10 %).

Bar histogram labelled QA-680, same axes. Peaked at <1.6 um (just below 30 %), next bin 1.6-2.0 um at about 20 %, monotonic decrease to the 4.4-4.8 um bin, then a clear secondary bar in >4.8 um (below 10 %), the largest >4.8 um bar of panels a-c.
Bar histogram labelled QA-740, same axes. Peak at <1.6 um at/just above the 30 % gridline, 1.6-2.0 um at about 20 %, decreasing tail, and a secondary rise in >4.8 um (just below 10 %).
Bar histogram labelled QA-800, same axes. Similar shape to (c): <1.6 um peak at/just above 30 %, then a monotonic decline across the intermediate bins, with a small rise in >4.8 um (just below 10 %).

observations.observation: The figure is a 2x2 grid of bar histograms with a shared horizontal axis d/um and a shared vertical axis Proportion/% (ticks 0-40, gridlines every 10).
Panels are labelled inside the top-right corner as QA-620 (a), QA-680 (b), QA-740 (c) and QA-800 (d).
In all four panels the tallest bar is the <1.6 um bin; it lies just below the 30 % gridline in (a) and (b) and at or slightly above the 30 % gridline in (c) and (d).
In all four panels the proportion decreases monotonically from the <1.6 um bin to the 4.4-4.8 um bin, i.e. count increases as grain size decreases.
Every panel shows a small secondary rise in the largest-size bin (>4.8 um) that stays below the 10 % gridline.
No numeric data labels are printed on the bars; values are only readable relative to the 0/10/20/30/40 % gridlines.

The caption calls the specimens 'OA specimens before tensile tests' and states d was obtained by the equivalent circle method from EBSD data, whereas the panel labels themselves read QA-620/QA-680/QA-740/QA-800.
The citing text states the figure shows austenitic grain size statistics of QA specimens before deformation and that all QA specimens share a similar distribution trend.

The citing text states that the size of around 90 % of the grains was less than 4.8 um; this is consistent with the small total bar height of the >4.8 um bin in each panel but is not printed on the figure.
The citing text links the fine austenite grains to higher alloy-element enrichment, higher austenitic stability, and the TRIP effect dominating hardening in stage III of work hardening.
